expectation: The real app window opens and the bridge reports StationAI API version 1.
Blank titles, missing roots, and unavailable roots cannot create a task.
A repository task creates a title-derived worktree and persists its repository, branch, path, and task state across fresh connections.
Creating a task for a branch with an existing worktree reuses that exact path.
A task selecting multiple repositories gets one correctly persisted worktree per repository.
A folder-only task remains usable and persists its context folder without repository worktrees.
A worktree already assigned to another active task is rejected without creating another task.
Moving a clean task to Done removes its worktree directory and keeps the Git branch.
A task with uncommitted work cannot move to Done and retains its active worktree.
Tasks move through each supported status; invalid status leaves the task unchanged.
A rename persists; rejecting a blank rename preserves the last valid title.
Root editing preserves order, removes duplicates, and rejects an empty list.
Deleting a task removes it from the board and future lookup returns not found.
The default parent can be read, changed, cleared, and an unavailable path is rejected.
Suggestions include top-level Git roots and skip nested repositories and symlink targets.
Clearing the default parent does not change roots already saved on a task.
A newly created task shows an empty conversation and has no stored messages or activity.
Blank drafts cannot be sent or stored; live responses can be paused, continued, and their task activity expanded.
The composer shows a Codex-reported model, while unsupported modes and malformed model IDs are rejected before creating history.
The task view separates staged and working Git changes, and selecting text or JSON files opens a calculated, highlighted side-by-side diff over the conversation.
External file edits and Git commits update the open task's changes sidebar automatically, and fresh CLI connections report the same Git status.
